$comment: Generated from docs/architecture/audit-actions.yaml by tools/gen/audit. Do not edit.

correlation.description: metadata.correlation_uid: the id of the call being served.

decimal.description: A count written as decimal digits: the generation of a data key, which OCSF's entity.version holds as a string.

hex64.description: A SHA-256 digest in lower-case hexadecimal.

hex96.description: A SHA-384 digest in lower-case hexadecimal.

ident.description: A name or an id of the registry, of a store address or of a key, never a value. Any character may come first, because the values are not alike: a key id is an RFC 7638 thumbprint in base64url and one in thirty-two begins with '-' or '_', a store part may begin with '.', and a policy @id may begin with '.', ':' or '/'. The domains are in kits/conformance/audit/domain-vectors.json, which both emitters validate.

lost.description: unmapped.sluis.lost: the running total of best-effort facts one process failed to deliver for the tenant of this record (ADR 0029). The emitter writes it; a caller cannot.

param_count.description: How many request parameters were read and ignored: at most one for each two bytes of the largest form body that entry reads (32 KiB), so the number is bounded by the request and holds no name.

peer_uid.description: The uid of a peer as the kernel read it, or -1 for a peer the registry does not know.

policy.description: The policy decision that gated the action (security_control profile): its id and the digest of the bundle.

pseudonym.description: user.uid: a keyed pseudonym of a person, never the person (ADR 0029, Pseudonyms).

reason.description: A status_code: the closed reason of a refusal. It names a rule and never a value; some actors word it in capitals.

tenant.description: A tenant id, or '*' for all the tenants of a grant: a store part (lower-case letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', never '.' or '..'), which may begin with any of them.

text.description: Bounded text. The emitter also refuses an e-mail shape in any string.

user_known.description: user of a record whose subject is known: the pseudonym, and what kind of identity it is (1 a person, 3 a client or a workload, 99 another kind), so a pseudonym of a client never passes for a person's.

user_unknown.description: user of an Authentication record that established no subject: OCSF requires the user, and this says there is none (ADR 0030, The OCSF attributes a class requires).

uuid7.description: metadata.uid: a UUIDv7 in the form of RFC 9562.

word.description: A closed word: a reason, an operation, a state.
